objective: Proof. The asymmetric knot x or (y != z), with signs and any order of places, has a pinning piece (four internal points, five lines), a pinned line x = 0 is a disequality, and a full piece exists, so by the pinning theorem deciding it on cubic systems is NP-complete. Verify the pieces by enumeration, check the reduction end to end on random instances, and record a census of its failures on small cubic systems.
status: Proved by PINNING-20261031-001B-P001: x or (y != z) (12 relations, signed, any order of places) has a pinning piece (four internal points, five lines, the shared skeleton), a disequality link and a full piece, so by the pinning theorem it is NP-complete on simple cubic systems; failures are absent on small systems (n <= 5 exhaustive, sampled to n = 10) but exist (an explicit 25-line system)
title: x or (y != z) pins, so it is NP-complete on cubic systems
